# Feature And Support Matrix

<!-- Generated by scripts/generate-support-matrix.mjs. Do not edit by hand. -->

This is the source-of-truth support page for the README and book. “Supported”
describes the primary JavaScript compiler unless a row explicitly names the
Lumen-written bootstrap compiler.

Regenerate it with `npm run docs:support`.

## Compiler Architecture

| Area | Status | Actual behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| JavaScript compiler pipeline | Supported | Primary compiler: tokenizer, parser, semantic analysis, type checking, typed IR validation, and LLVM lowering. |
| JavaScript compiler IR | Supported | Uses typed IR modules, functions, blocks, instructions, values, and terminators. The LLVM backend consumes this IR. |
| Lumen-written bootstrap compiler | Subset | Parses and compiles only the features and diagnostics listed in the parity tables below. |
| Bootstrap compiler IR | Partial | Uses typed Lumen structs for an IR summary, but still relies on a program map and statement compatibility bridge. It is not the JavaScript compiler typed IR. |
| Stage-2 and stage-3 bootstrap | Checkpoint | Stage-1 is built by the JavaScript compiler. Later stages reproduce its embedded LLVM checkpoint byte for byte and run the parity fixtures. |
| Full source self-hosting | Not Implemented | Compiling compiler/main.lm returns the embedded stage-1 LLVM image through compilerImage(). The bootstrap compiler does not regenerate itself from its source. |

## JavaScript/Bootstrap Parity Features

Each row is exercised across diagnostics, llvm, executable.

| Feature | Status | Fixture |

| variables, constants, strings, and println | Parity-tested subset | `examples/basic.lm` |
| binary expressions and if branching | Parity-tested subset | `examples/self-host-if-binary.lm` |
| helper function calls | Parity-tested subset | `examples/self-host-call.lm` |
| classic for loops and updates | Parity-tested subset | `examples/for-loop.lm` |
| while loops | Parity-tested subset | `examples/while-do.lm` |
| break, continue, interpolation, and else | Parity-tested subset | `examples/control-flow.lm` |
| data-driven loop names, values, and bounds | Parity-tested subset | `tests/bootstrap/generic-for.lm` |
| struct literals and field access | Parity-tested subset | `examples/struct.lm` |
| integer arrays and indexing | Parity-tested subset | `examples/self-host-array.lm` |
| simple async functions and await | Parity-tested subset | `examples/self-host-async.lm` |
| enums and match expressions | Parity-tested subset | `examples/self-host-enum-match.lm` |
| numeric switch cases and default | Parity-tested subset | `examples/self-host-switch.lm` |
| data-driven switch assignments | Parity-tested subset | `tests/bootstrap/generic-switch.lm` |
| throw and catch recovery | Parity-tested subset | `examples/self-host-try-catch.lm` |

Rows absent from the two parity tables are not claimed as bootstrap-compiler
support. The primary JavaScript compiler supports more language and runtime
features than the bootstrap subset.

## Platform Support

| Platform | Status | Actual behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| macOS | Targeted | Development target with Clang and POSIX runtime support. |
| Linux | Targeted | Has Linux argument, crypto, and WebSocket providers. Automated Linux CI is not present yet. |
| Windows | Unsupported | The native runtime and build flow require POSIX APIs and pthreads. |
